title: Migrate Go file-utils from deprecated io/ioutil to io and os packages
description: A Go file-utility package uses the deprecated io/ioutil package. Migrate all three functions to use the modern io and os equivalents added in Go 1.16.

task_spec.prompt:
The package internal/fileutil/fileutil.go uses the deprecated io/ioutil package in three functions:
  - ReadBytes: uses ioutil.ReadFile
  - WriteBytes: uses ioutil.WriteFile
  - ReadLines: uses ioutil.ReadFile

Migrate all three functions to use the modern equivalents (available since Go 1.16):
  - ioutil.ReadFile(path)  → os.ReadFile(path)
  - ioutil.WriteFile(path, data, perm) → os.WriteFile(path, data, perm)

Update the import block: remove 'io/ioutil', add 'os' if not already present.

Do NOT change the function signatures or return types. The 3 existing tests must still pass after the migration.

Run go test ./... to confirm. Run go build ./... to confirm.
success_criteria: No ioutil references remain in the file
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
